findings.summary: Two definitions are still repeated almost word for word, in the overview and the failure list
findings.evidence: In the overview: "A secondmate is a persistent [[home]], not a backlog item." The home Glossary entry: "A secondmate is a persistent home of its own, not an item in a backlog." In the limits: "...a local-only ship or a scout that records no PR keeps its place until cleanup." The place Glossary entry: "...a local-only ship or a scout keeps its place until cleanup...". The request says "Do not repeat the definition text in the overview ... or the failure list". The complaint behind it is repetition "almost word for word". Fix: cut the overview clause to "A secondmate is a persistent [[home]]" or drop it. End the limit after "free a [[place]]", or move the secondmate sentence out of the home definition.

findings.summary: Soundness: the test only catches exact copies of a definition sentence, so a lightly reworded copy passes
findings.evidence: It runs page.matches(sentence).count() == 1 on each whole sentence split on ". ". Both copies in the finding above pass it because a few words differ ("of its own", "an item in a backlog" vs "a backlog item"). The request is about near-verbatim repetition. A more correct check flags any long word run a definition shares with prose outside it (for example 6+ normalised words), or uses a token-overlap ratio per sentence.

summary: The change mostly works: yolo, green, red, in scope and captain are now defined only in "Words used first", place, places-held and home only in the Glossary, and new [[term]] markup renders as links to anchors that exist. The new tests pass, along with the existing xtask and study tests, and fmt, clippy and the full test suite pass in the recorded CI run. It still fails, for two reasons. First, the page repeats two definitions almost word for word in places the request names: the overview's "A secondmate is a persistent home, not a backlog item" matches a sentence in the home definition, and a failure-list item repeats the place definition's "a local-only ship or a scout keeps its place until cleanup". Second, the new test only looks for exact copies of whole sentences, so these reworded copies pass it. That is the near-verbatim repetition the request targets. The fix is to trim the two sentences and make the test catch shared runs of words rather than only identical sentences.
